doc.title: Mose Allison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Ole Miss, mechanical engineering and wanting out of Tippo
summary: Before the Army he studied engineering at Ole Miss to travel; his father preferred to stay home.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: To the guy who played “The Washington and Lee...” Now, before you went in the
Army, you spent a year or six months at University of Mississippi.
You were studying initially mechanical drawing and mechanical engineering?
Were you interested in the sciences or mathematics when you were in high school or as a kid? Did you have a proclivity for that?
No. I found out that it was a good thing to take, because chemical engineering, you went all over the world.
So you thought you could get yourself out of Tippo.
So at a certain point, you were thinking like your mother, like you want to get out of this place once in a while.
Did your father like to travel, too, or did he like to stay at home?
No, I don’t remember him traveling. We used to go to Booneville, which is a different part of the state. Booneville is ̀where my mother was born, and we used to go there every...
Even that was a long trip for your dad.
He liked staying home. I know she liked to travel.
